newsitem.title: USA: Investors scoop up corp debt issues, more to come.
newsitem.headline: Investors scoop up corp debt issues, more to come.

text.p: U.S. companies continued to tap the corporate bond new-issue market at a steady pace as investors stood by, ready to gobble up the paper, dealers said.
"Deals are still coming and the demand is still there," said a high-grade syndicate source.
Leading the new issue pack on Thursday is Brunswick Corp's expected $250 million Baa1/BBB-plus rated 10-year issue, via underwriter Merrill Lynch & Co.
Price talk on the Brunswick issue is seen at 65 basis points over comparable U.S. Treasuries, sources said.
Merrill Lynch is expected to underwrite Western Mining's $400 million two-tranche debt offering.
Price talk on Western Mining's 10-year issue is seen between 60 to 65 basis points over Treasuries while price talk on the 30-year tranche is in the area of 80 to 85 basis points over, sources added.
Dealers said despite a downturn in the Treasuries market, corporate debt deals should continue to flow in as issuers wrap up their financing needs for the year amid still attractive rates.
The benchmark 30-year Treasury bond was down 29/32 at 100-15/32 to yield 6.46 percent following Wednesday's close at 6.39 percent.
"The market's a litte weak today but deals should still come in light of the demand for the paper," another syndicate source said.
Also expected to price on Thursday is $100 million Baa3/BBB 10-year debt out of Spieker Properties. Price talk on the issue is in the area of 95 basis points over, sources said.
AES China Generating is expected to issue $180 million in a 10-year senior note offering via Morgan Stanely. Initial talk on the size of the deal was $150 million, dealers said.
In addition, Stuart Enterprises is expected to issue $100 million in seven-year debt via NationsBanc Capital Markets.
Among new issues trading in the secondary market, IBM's new 7.125 percent 100-year bonds were seen holding up well, according to sources.
"The issue was trading at 81 bid, 80 offer at the break and has held in right around the issue spread," a dealer said.

Dealers said despite the rise in U.S. Treasury yields, issuers pressed to get financing done before year-end will have to square away those deals now. However, they added, yields are still at their lowest since the spring.

"The problem is...that the year's coming to a close and although we're still at a very low (Treasury) yield level we're now off the highs," said one syndicate source. "People always want to hit the highs but that doesn't always happen."
Turning to the high-yield primary sector, a slew of new issues are set to come to market near term, dealers added.
AK Steel is getting set to bring $550 million 10-year 144A senior notes via CS First Boston, dealers said.
Phonetel Tech is expected to issue $110 million senior notes due 2006 via JP Morgan Securities.
Jacor Communications is expected to issue $125 million 10-year senior subordinated notes via Donaldson Lufkin & Jenrette.
Quest Diagnostics is expected to issue $150 million senior subordinated notes due 2006 via JP Morgan Securities.
Delta Beverage Group is also expected to issue $120 million seven-year 144A notes via NationsBanc.
--Nancy Leinfuss, 212-859-1675
